reviewedGap.title: Failed OAuth callbacks retain sensitive query URLs without the required response protections
reviewedGap.rationale: The callback controller sets no-store/no-referrer and redirects only after authorizations.callback succeeds. Invalid state, provider refusal, missing permissions, expired ownership and other failures throw before those headers are set. There is no general response protection in main.ts, AppModule or the inspected exception filter that supplies them. Consequently the browser can remain on a code/state-bearing callback URL with an ordinary error response. The spec asserts safe redirect headers only on success. This is a current CP2-SAFE-OUTPUT/callback contract gap; gateway logging parity remains the separately required CP4 responsibility.
reviewedGap.suggested_action: Apply callback confidentiality headers before validation and cover unsuccessful callback outcomes with a safe return path that removes code/state/provider error query data while retaining the appropriate safe failure classification. Include session/state/provider-error/expired cases and assert no sensitive value in Location or response body. Preserve the later mandatory gateway/query-log and real-browser verification rather than treating controller tests as that proof.
